subject: Setting up hierarchy file for AMOVA?

messages.author: 2089acceb5b8ed76
messages.subject: Setting up hierarchy file for AMOVA?
parts:
I am having trouble figuring out how to setup a hierarchy file for my hierarchical AMOVA analysis using SNPs, in which I have 3 species of insect herbivores collected from 3 host plants and 2 sites. From Justin Bagley's website his hierarchy file is setup as follows:

 ind pop drainind pop drain 
1 1 6 3
2 2 1 1

I understand the first column is individual, second is population, 3rd is the drain where he collected the fish from, but why pop and drain repeated again? Also there are 4 values per column even though there should be five?

So should I set mine up by each of the 3 species, with the following:

ind pop hostplant
1 1 1
2 2 3

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Setting up hierarchy file for AMOVA?
parts:
Hello Miles,

I'm assuming you are referring to this website? http://www.justinbagley.org/3007/running-amova-analysis-molecular-variance-biallelic-snp-data-r

I haven't seen it before, but it's nice to see that people are writing their own tutorials :)

To answer your questions:

From Justin Bagley's website his hierarchy file is setup as follows:

 ind pop drainind pop drain 
1 1 6 3
2 2 1 1

I understand the first column is individual, second is population, 3rd is the drain where he collected the fish from, but why pop and drain repeated again? Also there are 4 values per column even though there should be five?

I believe this may be a mistake in copy+paste. There are three columns in the data; the first "column" is simply the row numbers, which is the output from R. You can find a tutorial on how to handle strata here: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials and an example of using strata to examine population differentiation here: http://popgen.nescent.org/2015-12-15-microsatellite-differentiation.html

So should I set mine up by each of the 3 species, with the following:

ind pop hostplant
1 1 1
2 2 3

I would recommend for your strata to have four columns:

1. individual ID (this allows you to make sure your strata are in the same order as your data)
2. species
3. population
4. host

Moreover, I would additionally recommend to include meaningful names as opposed to numbers. 

Hope that helps!
Zhian
